checks: The parameter domain contains zero and is open and convex. Evaluating at the negative radial point of an inner ball gives the strict uniform radius bound. Local positivity of the denominator justifies both derivatives, and the positive-measure nonzero set of a nonzero linear form makes the Hessian positive definite.

At a boundary parameter the limiting affine function is nonnegative and must vanish somewhere. The zero point lies at positive distance from the fixed transverse disk plane. On the cone the Jacobian is that distance times t^(d−1); on t in [δ,2δ] the contribution is bounded below by a positive constant times δ^d/δ^(d+1). The same computation with the disk of unit zero-dimensional mass works for d=1. A minimizing sequence has a subsequential limit in the closure, and the bound excludes the boundary.

The stationary vector identity implies ∫(L−1)L^(−d−2)=0, and the two integrals are therefore equal to E. Dividing by E gives the mass, barycenter, and mean L, and strict positivity on a compact set gives the smooth positive extension.

The inverse w=v/(1−a·v) is defined on the image because 1−a·v=1/L. The derivative determinant is L^(−d)(1−(a·w)/L)=L^(−d−1). For x'=Qx+b, the mark translates with the body, Q^T bijects admissible parameters, and the volume factor is |det Q|.

For proper K⊊H, the segment from an exterior-to-K point of H toward an interior point of H gives a point in int H outside the closed K, hence a positive-volume ball in H\K. The attained H-parameter restricts to an admissible K-parameter and gives a strict inequality in the right direction. The mark is automatically interior to H.

A zero parameter gives ordinary volume. Its gradient vanishes exactly at the centroid, which lies in the interior because averaging any supporting affine form gives strict inequality from the support value. As an independent d=1 check, for K−y=[−r,s] with r,s>0 the objective is (r+s)/[(1−ar)(1+as)] and its minimum is 4rs/(r+s), attained at (s−r)/(2rs).
